1	# Model proposals and the pre-approval review (M3.1)
2	
3	How a coding agent hands VCV a typed model change, and how a reviewer sees exactly what it
4	would change before deciding. This is the first step of the model-first path in
5	[Issue #17](https://github.com/TheBluemist1404/vibe-code-visualiser/issues/17):
6	
7	1. the agent reads the model and the source evidence and **authors a typed proposal** (a YAML or
8	   JSON file of its own, outside `.vcv/`);
9	2. **VCV validates** it and records it as pending: `vcv proposal submit`;
10	3. **a separate reviewer** previews it (`vcv proposal preview`) and approves the exact digest
11	   with a trusted key (`vcv review approve`, see [approvals.md](approvals.md));
12	4. only an approved change becomes the next canonical `.vcv/` revision; implementation comes
13	   after that (M3.3).
14	
15	Design notes: [ADR 0008](adr/0008-model-first-changes.md).
16	
17	## Submitting: proposal-only
18	
19	```sh
20	vcv proposal submit <checkout> <change.yaml> [--json]
21	```
22	
23	The change file is the existing typed change shape (`ModelEngine.propose`, see
24	[ir-v0.2-conformance.md](ir-v0.2-conformance.md)):
25	
26	```yaml
27	changeId: chg-cancel-enrollment      # yours to choose; used once, never reused
28	projectId: prj-course-desk
29	expectedRevision: rev-1              # the revision you read; stale proposals are refused
30	rationale: A student can cancel a confirmed enrollment and is notified.
31	operations:
32	  - type: createCapability
33	    capability: { id: cap-cancel-enrollment, kind: capability, owner: mod-enrollment, name: Cancel an enrollment, initiatorActorId: act-student }
34	  - type: setRuleStatement
35	    ruleId: rul-announce-every-decision
36	    statement: Each enrollment decision or cancellation results in exactly one notification to the student.
37	```
38	
39	Operations: `createModule`, `createEvent`, `createCapability` (new in M3.1), `createRule`,
40	`addDataAttribute`, `addState`, `addTransition`, `renameObject`, `renameState`, `linkContract`,
41	`setModuleDependencies`, `removeObject`, `setRuleStatement`, `setDescription`, `approveDraft`.
42	There is no generic patch. The payload cannot name a proposer, approver or status.
43	
44	A proposal may also carry an `implementation` request: `behavior`, `acceptanceCriteria`, optional
45	`suggestedTests` and `scope` (repository-relative paths or globs). It is shown in the preview and
46	covered by the proposal digest, so the reviewer approves it together with the operations; the
47	engine never reads it. After approval it becomes the implementation handoff
48	([implementation.md](implementation.md)).
49	
50	`submit` is **proposal-only**. It narrows whatever permissions the host holds to
51	`model:propose` before calling the engine, so the result is always one of
52	
53	| Status | Recorded? | Meaning |
54	|---|---|---|
55	| `pending` | yes | Validated against the current revision; waiting for a separate reviewer. `.vcv/HEAD` did not move. |
56	| `rejected` | yes, for a well-formed proposal that fails validation (the record keeps the diagnostics); no, for a schema error, a replayed change ID or an oversized proposal | Fix it and submit under a **new** change ID. |
57	| `denied` | no | The host may not propose. |
58	
59	It never applies or approves, even for a host holding `model:apply` and `model:approve`, and the
60	result reports `.vcv/HEAD` before and after the call (always equal). `vcv propose <store>` keeps
61	its old behavior for hosts that apply directly; give agents `vcv proposal submit`.
62	
63	Limits on this surface: at most 100 operations and 256 KB (canonical JSON) per proposal.
64	
65	Each diagnostic has `code`, `severity`, `path`, `message` and, for the common codes, a `hint`
66	saying what to do (`STALE_REVISION`: re-read and resubmit against the current revision;
67	`DUPLICATE_CHANGE`: change IDs are immutable, pick a new one; `TARGET_MISSING`, `UNKNOWN_REF`,
68	`ID_IN_USE`, `REFERENCED`, `DEPENDENCY_CYCLE`, `SCHEMA`, `TOO_LARGE`, ...).
69	
70	### Proposal identity
71	
72	A proposal is identified by its change ID (used once; a replay never overwrites the original
73	record) and by its **proposal digest**: sha256 over the canonical JSON of the change exactly as
74	submitted. The digest is derived, never stored, and the same for a dry run and for the recorded
75	proposal, so a reviewer can bind a decision to the content they saw (`vcv review approve --digest`, see [approvals.md](approvals.md)).
76	
77	## Reviewing: preview
78	
79	```sh
80	vcv proposal preview <checkout> <changeId> [--json] [--limit n]
81	vcv proposal preview <checkout> --file <change.yaml> [--json]      # dry run, nothing recorded
82	```
83	
84	MCP (`vcv-mcp --repo <checkout>`): `vcv_preview_proposal` with `{ changeId }` or `{ change }`.
85	
86	Read-only: nothing is written, not even store recovery. The result has
87	
88	| Section | Content |
89	|---|---|
90	| `proposal` | change ID, digest, origin (`record` or `unsubmitted`), lifecycle, proposer, base revision, rationale, one line per operation |
91	| `validation` | the engine's own `checkChange` against this checkout's revision **now** (`appliesToCurrent`, errors and warnings with hints), and the diagnostics stored at submission |
92	| `delta` | the object-level before/after change: added, removed and modified objects with the changed fields (values capped at 300 characters). Against the current revision when the change applies; against its base revision when it is stale; `null` when it applies to neither |
93	| `impact` | modules owning a changed object (`changed`) or a structural impact candidate (`impacted`), `crossModule` (`yes`, `no`, or `not-determined` when only one module was seen but the candidate list was cut), contracts, and `@vcv/query` impact candidates with one dependency path each |
94	| `bindings` | binding claims on changed, removed or impacted objects: code that probably has to change too. Listed, not verified; use `vcv evidence` for their state |
95	| `states` | `change` (lifecycle), `approval` (`none`, `applied-by-host`, `approved-by-separate-reviewer`), `snapshotStatus` and `implementation`, kept apart |
96	| `assumptions` | what nobody has checked: structural impact is not semantic proof, the code was not compared, the proposer identity is a host assertion, and case-specific ones (no rationale, stale, cross-module, truncated, no claims) |
97	
98	Every list is capped by `limit` (default 50, max 200) with `total` and `truncated`.
99	
100	**One observation per call.** A preview (and a listing) reads the project status, the model and
101	its history, the change records and, for a preview, the binding claims once, and reports only
102	what it read then; `context` describes that same revision. Before answering it checks the store
103	fingerprint, the Git commit, the change records and the claim files again. If anything moved (a
104	`git checkout`, an edit of `.vcv/`), the call fails with `STATE_CHANGED` and nothing is mixed:
105	retry. There are no locks, watchers or writes.
106	
107	**Untrusted files are not followed.** HEAD, revision files and change records are read only as
108	regular files (never through a symlink, never a FIFO or device), up to a size bound (4 MB HEAD,
109	8 MB revision, 1 MB change record), and `revisions/` and `changes/` must be plain directories.
110	An entry that breaks this, or a change record that is not valid JSON for its own ID, makes the
111	project `invalid` everywhere (status, CLI, MCP, the writer), naming the file: recovery relies on
112	reading every applied record, so it cannot be skipped. A readable record whose `change` is not a
113	typed change only shows as lifecycle `invalid`; the project stays usable.
114	
115	## Lifecycle and the states that must not be confused
116	
117	```sh
118	vcv proposal list <checkout> [--states pending,stale,rejected,applied,invalid] [--json]
119	```
120	
121	MCP: `vcv_list_proposals`. The lifecycle is derived from the record and this checkout's model
122	every time; it is never stored:
123	
124	| Lifecycle | Meaning |
125	|---|---|
126	| `pending` | validated, awaiting a separate reviewer; base revision is the current one |
127	| `stale` | still pending, but the checkout's model is no longer its base: `superseded` (the base is an earlier revision of this line) or `other-line` (the base is not in this checkout's history, e.g. a record from another branch). An approval would fail with `STALE_REVISION`; submit a new proposal |
128	| `rejected` | failed validation at submission or when an approval rechecked it |
129	| `applied` | committed as a model revision; `resultInThisCheckout` says whether this checkout's history contains it |
130	| `invalid` | the record file does not hold a typed change |
131	
132	Four things are reported separately and none implies another:
133	
134	- **change approval** (`approval`, `recordedApproverId`): what the change record says.
135	  `applied-by-host` means it was applied without a separate approver (a host with
136	  `model:apply`, or a self-approval the policy allowed); `approved-by-separate-reviewer` means
137	  the record names an approver other than the proposer. Either way a record in a Git
138	  repository is not proof that a particular person approved it; a signed attestation checked by
139	  `vcv integrity` is ([approvals.md](approvals.md)).
140	- **snapshot status** (`snapshotStatus`, draft or approved): the model's own `approveDraft`
141	  flag. Approving a change does not approve a draft snapshot, and vice versa.
142	- **binding resolution** (`vcv evidence`): whether a pointer into the code resolves. Not model
143	  approval, not correctness.
144	- **implementation**: always `not-recorded` here. VCV never infers that approved intent was
145	  implemented; the implementing agent's report is a separate claim
146	  ([implementation.md](implementation.md)).
147	
148	## What this does not do
149	
150	No MCP write tools (submission is the host's CLI), no approval here (that is
151	`vcv review approve`, [approvals.md](approvals.md)), no implementation handoff
152	(M3.3), no reconciliation of code and model (M4). VCV never writes a proposal itself: the agent
153	authors it, VCV validates and records it.
154	# Maintaining a VCV model after the code changed
155	
156	This guide is for a coding agent (or a person) keeping an existing VCV model in line with a
157	repository whose code has changed. It is general: it says nothing about any particular
158	application. It assumes the repository already has a `.vcv/` project and binding claims.
159	
160	**Who does what.**
161	
162	| | does | does not |
163	|---|---|---|
164	| **You** | read the evidence, inspect the code, decide what the change means, and propose a typed model change | edit `.vcv/` files, approve your own change, or present a guess as a fact |
165	| **VCV** | reports which claims still resolve and whether their code or model object changed; validates your proposal and stores it as pending | analyse what code means, infer a model change, edit the model by itself, or watch the repository |
166	| **A person** | reviews and approves (or rejects) the pending proposal | |
167	
168	`vcv` below is the VCV command line. In a VCV checkout it is
169	`npm run vcv -- <args>` (or `node --experimental-strip-types apps/cli/src/main.ts <args>`).
170	The same evidence is available over MCP (`vcv-mcp --repo <checkout>`, tools
171	`vcv_get_evidence_overview`, `vcv_get_object_evidence`, `vcv_get_binding_evidence`,
172	`vcv_refresh_evidence`) with identical requests and results.
173	
174	## Workflow
175	
176	1. **Check the project.** `vcv project status .` must report `ready`. Note the model revision
177	   (for example `rev-1 [draft]`) and whether the working tree is dirty.
178	2. **Recheck the evidence.** `vcv evidence . refresh` recomputes every claim against the working
179	   tree now and prints counts by state and an `observationToken`. Nothing runs in the background:
180	   evidence is only as new as your last call.
181	3. **List what needs a look.** `vcv evidence . overview --states stale,missing,ambiguous,indeterminate,invalid`.
182	   For each model object named there, `vcv evidence . object <id>` shows every claim about it,
183	   and `vcv query .vcv context <id>` shows the model's current record of it.
184	4. **Inspect the code yourself.** `git status`, `git diff` and `git log` show what changed; read
185	   the files named in the claims' locators and the tests. Evidence tells you *where* to look and
186	   *that* something changed, never *what it means*. A claim's `locator.detail` and
187	   `freshness.*.cause` say why it is in its state.
188	5. **Decide what is no longer true in the model.** Compare each affected object's record (its
189	   statement, description, attributes, states) with the code. Model what the code does now. If
190	   the code and its tests disagree, or you cannot tell, say so instead of choosing.
191	6. **Write one proposed change** to a file outside `.vcv/` (for example
192	   `vcv-maintenance/change.yaml`) using the operations below, with `expectedRevision` set to the
193	   current model revision and a `rationale` that cites the code.
194	7. **Submit it**: `vcv propose .vcv vcv-maintenance/change.yaml`. As an agent you can propose but
195	   not apply, so a valid change is stored as `pending` for a person. `rejected` comes with
196	   diagnostics: fix the change file and submit again under a new `changeId`. Do not try to
197	   approve it; an approval attempt by the proposer is denied.
198	8. **Check again.** `vcv evidence . refresh --since <token>` should still report the same
199	   claims as stale or missing: a pending proposal changes nothing, and claims are never updated
200	   by a model change. A person re-records or reasserts claims after reviewing the code.
201	9. **Write a report** next to the change (for example `vcv-maintenance/report.md`) that keeps
202	   four kinds of statement apart:
203	   - **Source observed**: what the code and its history show, with file paths;
204	   - **Agent inferred**: what you concluded it means for the model, and how sure you are;
205	   - **VCV validated**: what VCV reported (evidence states and causes, the proposal's status
206	     and diagnostics), quoted from its output;
207	   - **Needs a person**: the approval, claims to reassert or remove, and open questions.
208	
209	Never create, edit or delete files inside `.vcv/` yourself, and do not change the source code
210	or the claims unless you were asked to.
211	
212	## Evidence states
213	
214	| State | Meaning | Usual next step |
215	|---|---|---|
216	| `resolved` | the pointer resolves to exactly one artifact, and neither its code nor the model object changed since the claim | nothing, but it is not proof the code is correct |
217	| `stale` | it resolves, but the selected code changed (`source: changed`) or the model object changed or was removed (`model: changed/removed`) | read the code; propose a model change if the model is now wrong |
218	| `missing` | the file or selector no longer resolves (renamed, moved, deleted) | find where it went; a person reasserts or removes the claim |
219	| `ambiguous` | the selector matches more than one artifact | a person makes the locator more specific |
220	| `unchecked` | outside the supported subset (see below); only the claim is reported | inspect by hand |
221	| `indeterminate` | it resolves but some evidence is unknown (for example the claim's revision is from another branch) | treat as unknown, never as a pass |
222	| `invalid` | the claim file itself cannot be read (conflict markers, bad JSON, unsafe entry) | a person repairs the claim file |
223	
224	Every result says `meaning: "unverified"` and every claim `approval.approved: false`. The model's
225	own status (`context.snapshotStatus`, draft or approved) is a separate fact: a draft model with
226	resolved claims is still a draft, and an approved model with stale claims is still approved.
227	
228	An edit elsewhere in a bound file is reported as `fileChanged: true` with the cause "not
229	evidence about this claim"; only a change to the selected declaration (its tokens, not comments
230	or formatting) makes a symbol, route or test claim stale.
231	
232	## Change operations
233	
234	A change file:
235	
236	```yaml
237	changeId: ch-maint-01            # lowercase letters, digits, '.', '-', '_'; new for every submission
238	projectId: <the project id>      # from `vcv project status .`
239	expectedRevision: <current rev>  # e.g. rev-1
240	rationale: <why, citing the code>
241	operations:
242	  - type: setRuleStatement
243	    ruleId: rul-order-limit
244	    statement: An order of more than ten items is split into parcels of at most ten.
245	```
246	
247	| Operation | Parameters |
248	|---|---|
249	| `setRuleStatement` | `ruleId`, `statement` |
250	| `setDescription` | `objectId`, `description` (any object with a description, and the project; not attributes, states or transitions) |
251	| `createRule` | `rule`: a full rule object (`id`, `kind: rule`, `owner`, `name?`, `ruleKind`, `statement` …) |
252	| `renameObject` | `objectId`, `name` |
253	| `addDataAttribute` | `dataId`, `attribute: { id, name, type, nullable?, refDataId? }` |
254	| `createEvent` | `event: { id, kind: event, owner, name, description? }` |
255	| `createModule` | `module`: a full module object |
256	| `addState` / `renameState` | `behaviorId`, `state: { id, name }` / `behaviorId`, `stateId`, `name` |
257	| `addTransition` | `behaviorId`, `transition` (see the bootstrap guide's model reference) |
258	| `linkContract` | `moduleId`, `contractId` (adds a consumed contract) |
259	| `setModuleDependencies` | `moduleId`, `dependsOn: [module ids]` |
260	| `removeObject` | `objectId` (refused while anything still references it) |
261	
262	Operations apply in order, all or nothing, and the result must be a valid model. Prefer the
263	smallest change that makes the model true again; say in the rationale what you left unchanged
264	on purpose.
265	
266	## What evidence can and cannot tell you
267	
268	- Selectors are checked only in TypeScript (`.ts`, `.tsx`, `.mts`, `.cts`): named declarations,
269	  decorated HTTP handlers with literal paths, and `describe`/`it`/`test` titles. Everything else
270	  is `unchecked`. Only syntax is read; there is no type checking or import following.
271	- Routes are controller-relative: a global prefix or versioning is not applied.
272	- Test titles are matched by name; a renamed test is `missing`, even if it tests the same thing.
273	- VCV never follows a rename or a move. It reports `missing` and leaves the claim alone.
274	- `stale` says the code changed, not how. The diff and your reading decide what it means.
275	- A claim made against a model revision from another branch is `indeterminate` here.
276	- Evidence never contains source text or absolute paths, and reading it never writes anything.
277	# Implementation handoff and the implementation report (M3.3)
278	
279	The third step of the model-first path in
280	[Issue #17](https://github.com/TheBluemist1404/vibe-code-visualiser/issues/17). Once a change is
281	approved ([approvals.md](approvals.md)), the person invokes their coding agent, with its normal
282	tools, to implement it in the feature checkout. VCV gives that agent a bounded brief, the
283	**handoff**. Afterwards it records the agent's account next to what VCV can observe, in the
284	**implementation report**. VCV never starts the agent, never runs the tests, and never turns code
285	into model operations.
286	
287	Design notes: [ADR 0008](adr/0008-model-first-changes.md#m33-decisions).
288	
289	## The implementation request, approved with the change
290	
291	What should be implemented is part of the proposal, so the reviewer approves it together with the
292	operations and the proposal digest covers it:
293	
294	```yaml
295	changeId: chg-capacity
296	projectId: prj-course-desk
297	expectedRevision: rev-1
298	rationale: students asked why they were rejected
299	operations:
300	  - { type: setRuleStatement, ruleId: rul-seat-limit, statement: "…" }
301	implementation:
302	  behavior: When a course is full, the rejection tells the student the course's capacity.
303	  acceptanceCriteria:
304	    - A COURSE_FULL rejection includes the course capacity
305	    - Enrolling into a course with free seats is unchanged
306	  suggestedTests:
307	    - "EnrollmentService: rejects an enrollment into a full course and reports the capacity"
308	  scope: ["server/src/enrollment/**"]
309	```
310	
311	`scope` holds repository-relative paths or globs (`*`, `**`, `?`; a plain path also covers
312	everything below it). Absolute paths, `..` and backslashes are refused. The request is strict and
313	bounded: behavior up to 4000 characters, at most 30 criteria, 30 tests and 50 scope entries. The
314	engine never reads it. `vcv proposal preview` shows it, and warns when it is missing or declares no
315	scope.
316	
317	## The handoff: `vcv handoff <path> <changeId>`
318	
319	The handoff is printed as JSON. It is read-only and needs an **applied change with an
320	attestation whose signature verifies against its record**. Otherwise you get `NOT_APPLIED`,
321	`NOT_ATTESTED` or `NOT_IN_HISTORY` (check out the branch the change was approved on). Key trust
322	is not decided here; that is the host gate's job.
323	
324	It contains:
325	
326	| Field | What it is |
327	| ----- | ---------- |
328	| `change` | Change ID, proposal digest, base and approved revision, proposer, approver, rationale and operation summaries (display text, cut with `rationaleTruncated` / `operationsTruncated`; the proposal digest covers the full text) |
329	| `approval` | `valid-signature`, the key fingerprint, and `trustVerification: caller-asserted` |
330	| `modelNow` | The current revision; whether it is still the approved one; any later revisions (not covered) |
331	| `delta`, `impact` | The object-level before/after of the approved revisions, plus structural impact (modules, contracts, cross-module) |
332	| `request` | The approved implementation request, or null (a caveat then says there are no approved criteria) |
333	| `scope` | `declared` (the approved scope), and `fromBindings`: files that binding claims on changed or impacted objects point at |
334	| `tests` | Requested tests, plus `tests` claims on the affected objects |
335	| `bindings` | Each affected claim verified now (`resolved` / `stale` / `missing` …, with source and model freshness). `reassertAfterImplementing` marks claims on changed objects |
336	| `git` | Base commit, branch and dirty flag of the checkout the agent starts from, and `worktree`: a digest of the bytes seen (bound source files and files changed since HEAD) |
337	| `steps`, `caveats` | Fixed instructions and what the handoff does not establish |
338	| `digest` | sha256 over the canonical JSON of everything above |
339	
340	Properties:
341	
342	- **Deterministic.** There are no timestamps and the ordering is stable, so the same checkout
343	  state gives the same bytes and the same digest.
344	- **Bounded.** Strings and lists are capped, each cut marked. The printed handoff (2-space JSON,
345	  digest included) never exceeds 128 KiB: derived lists are halved until it fits, and if it still
346	  does not, the call fails with `HANDOFF_TOO_LARGE` instead.
347	- **Redacted.** Only repository-relative paths appear. The checkout's absolute path and the home
348	  directory are scrubbed from every string, including free text.
349	- **One observation.** Like every read surface, it reads the checkout once and rechecks before
350	  answering (`STATE_CHANGED`). The recheck covers the model store, the Git commit, the change
351	  records, the binding claims, the change's attestation, and the working tree: the set of changed
352	  files and the bytes of every changed or bound file. An edit during binding verification is
353	  never mixed into the result.
354	
355	## Implementing (the agent's job)
356	
357	The handoff's `steps` say it. The agent:
358	
359	- works in this checkout and inspects the code itself;
360	- stays in the declared scope;
361	- never edits `.vcv/HEAD`, `revisions/`, `changes/` or `approvals/`;
362	- if the approved model turns out to be wrong, stops and starts a **new** proposal and review;
363	- re-inspects and **reasserts** every claim marked `reassertAfterImplementing`
364	  (`vcv binding reassert … --expect <digest>`, or `vcv binding add` for new code). Reassertion is
365	  its claim, not an approval;
366	- runs the tests and writes down what really happened.
367	
368	## The report: `vcv implementation record <path> --report <file> [--expect <digest>]`
369	
370	The agent writes a JSON file of its own:
371	
372	```json
373	{
374	  "changeId": "chg-capacity",
375	  "baseCommit": "<git.baseCommit from the handoff>",
376	  "handoffDigest": "<digest from the handoff>",
377	  "testsRun": [{ "command": "npm test -w server", "outcome": "passed", "summary": "12 passed" }],
378	  "acceptance": [{ "criterion": "A COURSE_FULL rejection includes the course capacity", "status": "met", "evidence": "enrollment.service.ts" }],
379	  "gaps": ["the web UI does not show the capacity yet"],
380	  "outOfScope": [{ "path": "README.md", "reason": "documented the new message" }],
381	  "confidence": "medium"
382	}
383	```
384	
385	VCV records `.vcv/implementations/<changeId>.json` (commit it with the code). The report keeps
386	four sections apart, and none implies another:
387	
388	- **`approvedIntent`**: the approved request and operations, from the change record.
389	- **`agentClaims`**: tests, outcomes, criteria, gaps, explanations and confidence, with
390	  `claimedBy` (the host-asserted principal) and `verifiedByVcv: false`. VCV ran nothing and
391	  verified none of it.
392	- **`vcvObserved`**: what VCV sees:
393	  - source files changed since the base commit (committed, staged, unstaged and untracked);
394	  - those outside the approved scope;
395	  - `.vcv/` changes by area;
396	  - `worktree`: a digest of the bytes of every changed and bound file (content hashes, or size and
397	    mtime past the budget, then `complete: false`), so the report names one concrete dirty source
398	    state, not only file names. A path through a symlink is resolved like the binding verifier
399	    resolves it (inside the checkout only) and identified by its target's bytes, Git-ignored
400	    targets included;
401	  - each affected binding claim verified now, with `reasserted` (claimed at the approved revision
402	    or later).
403	- **`notReconciled`**: always `not-reconciled`. Whether the code implements the model is M4's
404	  reconciliation.
405	
406	It **warns rather than passes silently**:
407	
408	| Warning | When |
409	| ------- | ---- |
410	| `OUT_OF_SCOPE` | A file changed outside the approved scope; listed even when the agent explains it |
411	| `SCOPE_NOT_DECLARED` | The approved request declared no scope |
412	| `NO_IMPLEMENTATION_REQUEST` | The approved change carried no request |
413	| `NO_SOURCE_CHANGES` | No source file changed since the base commit |
414	| `BINDING_NOT_RESOLVED` | An affected claim is not `resolved` now |
415	| `BINDING_NOT_REASSERTED` | A claim on a changed object was last made before the approved revision |
416	| `NO_BINDINGS` | No claim points at the affected objects |
417	| `TEST_FAILED` | A reported test failed or errored |
418	| `NO_TESTS_RUN` | The agent reports no test run |
419	| `CRITERION_NOT_MET` / `CRITERION_UNKNOWN` | The agent reports a criterion as not met or unknown |
420	| `CRITERION_UNADDRESSED` | An approved criterion is not addressed in the report |
421	| `GAP` | The agent's own gaps |
422	| `MODEL_MOVED` | The model is past the approved revision |
423	| `STORE_FILES_CHANGED` | Unexpected `.vcv/` files changed |
424	| `CLAIMS_UNVERIFIED` | Always present |
425	
426	Recording changes no model state. The base commit must be in the repository and an ancestor of
427	HEAD (`UNKNOWN_COMMIT`). A second report is refused (`REPORT_EXISTS`). To replace a report, pass
428	the current file's digest with `--expect` (`REPORT_CHANGED` if it moved, including when another
429	report is written while the replacement is prepared: the file is re-read right before the
430	rename). A symlinked or non-directory `.vcv/implementations/` is refused (`UNSAFE_PATH`). Reports
431	are bounded to 256 KB and redacted like the handoff. Recording rechecks the same state as the
432	handoff (store, commit, records, claims, attestation, changed files and their bytes) before it
433	writes (`STATE_CHANGED`).
434	
435	`vcv implementation show <path> <changeId>` reads a report and recomputes VCV's observations now.
436	The stored report is validated against the full report schema first; a malformed or foreign file
437	is `INVALID_RECORD`, with the failing fields. `changedSinceReport` says whether the files, their
438	bytes, the scope or the binding states moved on since the report was recorded (an edit of an
439	already-dirty file counts), and `warningsNow` lists the warnings as they stand now.
440	
441	## What this does not do
442	
443	- No universal implementation verifier.
444	- No agent orchestration or hidden trigger of code generation.
445	- No test execution by VCV.
446	- No automatic model operations from code.
447	- No MCP tools for these (the agent uses the CLI it already has).
448	- No reconciliation (M4).
449	
450	The report is evidence for a human reviewer of the PR, not a gate.
451	# Source bindings (M2.4)
452	
453	A **binding claim** says that a piece of source code implements, exposes, persists or tests an
454	object in the model. An agent or a person makes the claim. VCV stores it, checks it and shows it.
455	VCV does **not** decide whether the code does what the claim says.
456	
457	Design contract: [ADR 0007 §§4–6](adr/0007-repository-projects.md). Tracking issue:
458	[#13](https://github.com/TheBluemist1404/vibe-code-visualiser/issues/13).
459	
460	## Three different things
461	
462	| | Who supplies it | What it means | What it does not mean |
463	|---|---|---|---|
464	| **Claim** | an agent or a person, through `vcv binding add` / `reassert` | "this code is that model object", plus who said so, when (model revision, Git commit) and why | that VCV checked the meaning, or that the code is correct |
465	| **Verification** | VCV, recomputed on every `vcv binding verify` | the pointer resolves to exactly one artifact, and whether that artifact or the model object changed since the claim | anything about behaviour. Every result carries `meaning: "unverified"` and `approved: false` |
466	| **Approval** | a person, through the model engine | a consequential model decision was accepted | binding claims are never approved by verification, and recording a claim never changes the model |
467	
468	Recording a claim does not make a draft model approved, and does not set the query API's
469	`implementationChecked` (it stays `false`).
470	
471	## Where claims live
472	
473	One file per claim: `.vcv/bindings/<bindingId>.json`, tracked by Git like the code. Git is the
474	only history: there is no binding revision counter, and no binding operation touches
475	`.vcv/HEAD`, the model revisions or the change records. A source edit and the matching claim
476	update can go into one commit.
477	
478	```json
479	{
480	  "format": 1,
481	  "bindingId": "impl.cap-enroll",
482	  "modelObjectId": "cap-enroll",
483	  "relation": "implements",
484	  "locator": { "path": "server/src/enrollment/enrollment.service.ts", "selector": { "kind": "symbol", "name": "EnrollmentService.enrollStudent" } },
485	  "provenance": { "source": "human", "principalId": "user:reviewer" },
486	  "modelRevision": "rev-1",
487	  "observed": {
488	    "commit": "917dffb9a9d4…",
489	    "workingTree": "modified",
490	    "fingerprint": { "algorithm": "vcv-fp-1", "file": "ceb0308c…", "selector": "418a1198…" }
491	  }
492	}
493	```
494	
495	(full file: [samples/m2.4-bindings/impl.cap-enroll.json](samples/m2.4-bindings/impl.cap-enroll.json))
496	
497	- `bindingId` uses the persisted-ID grammar. If you leave it out, it is derived from the relation,
498	  the object ID and a hash of the locator, so the same claim made on two branches has the same ID
499	  and the same bytes. It is kept when the claim is reasserted.
500	- `provenance.source` and `principalId` come from the host (the CLI's `--source` and `--as`),
501	  never from the claim payload. `confidence` is the claimant's own estimate; VCV never computes it.
502	- `observed` records what was inspected: the Git commit, whether the file differed from it, and
503	  fingerprints. There are no absolute paths and no timestamps; files are byte-for-byte
504	  deterministic (fixed key order).
505	- `disputed` is only set by `vcv binding dispute`; verification never sets it.
506	
507	## Locators
508	
509	A locator is a repository-relative POSIX path plus a selector:
510	
511	| Form | Selector | Checked in |
512	|---|---|---|
513	| `path` | whole file | any regular file |
514	| `path#symbol:Class.member` | named declaration: top-level `class`, `function`, `interface`, `type`, `enum`, variable; class methods, properties, accessors and `constructor`; interface members | `.ts` `.tsx` `.mts` `.cts` |
515	| `path#route:POST /orders/:id` | NestJS handler: `@Controller(path)` + `@Get/@Post/@Put/@Patch/@Delete/@Head/@Options/@All(path)` with literal paths | `.ts` `.tsx` `.mts` `.cts` |
516	| `path#test:Suite > case` | `describe`/`suite` and `it`/`test` titles with literal strings, outermost first (`.only`, `.skip`, `.todo`, `.concurrent` are fine) | `*.test.*` and `*.spec.*` |
517	
518	In JSON, a symbol selector can name its declaration kind (`"declaration": "class"`) and a route
519	selector its handler (`"handler": "OrdersController.place"`), to tell same-named artifacts apart.
520	
521	**Paths.** A path must already be normalized. These are refused with `UNSAFE_PATH`: an absolute
522	path, `..`, `.`, `//`, a backslash, anything under `.git/`, `.vcv/` or `node_modules/`, and a
523	symlink that leads out of the checkout. A path that differs from a file only by letter case is
524	reported, not matched, so case-insensitive filesystems behave like Linux.
525	
526	**Parser.** Only syntax is read, with the TypeScript 6 compiler API (`createSourceFile`), pinned
527	in `@vcv/repo`. There is no type checking, import following or project configuration. The
528	repository's own type checker is TypeScript 7, whose JS API is unstable and runs a native binary
529	over IPC, so it is not used here.
530	
531	## Verification states
532	
533	| State | Meaning |
534	|---|---|
535	| `resolved` | the selector matches exactly one artifact, its code is known to match the recorded fingerprint, and the bound model object is known not to have changed since the claim's revision. All evidence must be known; this is the only state `vcv binding verify` exits 0 for |
536	| `stale` | it still resolves, but the selected code changed (`source: changed`), or the model object changed or was removed (`model: changed`/`removed`). Someone should look again; it is not a contradiction |
537	| `missing` | the path or selector does not resolve (renamed, moved, deleted), or the path is no longer safe |
538	| `ambiguous` | the selector matches more than one artifact; none is picked |
539	| `indeterminate` | the selector resolves, nothing is known to have changed, but some evidence is unknown: the project is not `ready`, the claim's revision is not in this checkout's history, or the claim's fingerprint scheme is not one this VCV knows. Not a pass |
540	| `unchecked` | the file type or the construct is outside the subset above, so only the claim is reported |
541	| `invalid` | the claim entry is not a readable claim: conflict markers, bad JSON, wrong shape, a file name that does not match its `bindingId`, or an entry that is not read at all (a symlink, directory, special file, or a file over 64 KiB) |
542	
543	Each result has a separate `source` and `model` freshness, each with a cause:
544	
545	- **Source** compares the selected declaration's fingerprint: the sequence of its syntax tokens,
546	  including decorators but not comments, JSDoc or formatting. An edit elsewhere in the same file
547	  is reported as `fileChanged: true` with the cause "not evidence about this claim", and the
548	  claim stays `resolved`. A `file` selector compares the whole file (CRLF normalized to LF).
549	- Uncommitted edits count: verification reads the working tree, not the commit.
550	- **Model** compares the bound object between the claim's revision and the current one. If the
551	  claim's revision is not in this checkout's history (another branch), the state is `unknown`.
552	- **Git** context is reported (`commitMoved`, the file's working-tree state), but a moved commit
553	  alone never makes a claim stale.
554	
555	VCV never relocates a claim. After a rename or move, the claim reports `missing` until an agent
556	or a person reasserts it.
557	
558	## Writes are checkout-safe
559	
560	Every write names the claim it expects to find on disk: no claim for `add`, and the claim's
561	digest (from `vcv binding list`) for `reassert`, `remove` and `dispute`. The operation then:
562	
563	1. takes one snapshot: the project must be `ready`, and the snapshot holds the model store's
564	   fingerprint, the Git commit and the claim file's digest;
565	2. refuses unless the claim on disk is the expected one (`BINDING_EXISTS` for a create,
566	   `BINDING_CHANGED` or `NOT_FOUND` otherwise). This is how a claim read on one branch cannot
567	   overwrite another branch's same-ID claim after `git checkout`;
568	3. validates the claim: the model object exists at the current revision and at the claim's
569	   revision, the revision is in HEAD's history, the path is safe, and the locator resolves to
570	   exactly one artifact (`LOCATOR_MISSING`, `LOCATOR_AMBIGUOUS`, `LOCATOR_UNCHECKED`);
571	4. immediately before writing, re-checks the store fingerprint, the Git commit, the claim file and
572	   the source file's bytes. If any changed, it refuses with `STATE_CHANGED` and writes nothing;
573	5. writes through a temporary file and rename.
574	
575	**Reads stay inside the checkout too.** `.vcv/` and `.vcv/bindings/` must be plain directories:
576	if either is a symlink, every binding read and write refuses with `UNSAFE_PATH` before reading
577	anything (the model itself is still served). Each claim entry is read only if it is a regular,
578	non-symlink file of at most 64 KiB, opened with `O_NOFOLLOW` where the OS has it and checked
579	again on the open file. Anything else is listed as `invalid` with a reason and a stable
580	`unsafe:<kind>` digest: a symlinked entry can be removed or replaced as a link (its target is
581	never touched), while a directory or special file under a claim's name is left for a person.
582	Source files for selectors are size-checked before they are read (at most 1 MB is parsed);
583	whole-file fingerprints are streamed in 1 MiB chunks.
584	
585	As with model commits, this is check-then-rename, not a lock: a checkout landing inside the
586	rename itself is not prevented.
587	
588	Permissions (from the host): `binding:record` to add, reassert and remove; `binding:dispute` to
589	dispute. The CLI grants both by default, like the model permissions.
590	
591	## CLI
592	
593	```sh
594	vcv binding add <repo> --source agent --as agent:me --object cap-enroll --relation implements \
595	  --locator 'server/src/enrollment/enrollment.service.ts#symbol:EnrollmentService.enroll' \
596	  [--id impl.cap-enroll] [--rationale '…'] [--confidence 0.8] [--revision rev-1] [--allow-unchecked]
597	vcv binding list <repo> [--json]                       # IDs, digests, locators
598	vcv binding verify <repo> [bindingId] [--json]         # exit 0 only if every claim is resolved
599	vcv binding reassert <repo> <bindingId> --source human --expect <digest> --locator '<new locator>'
600	vcv binding dispute <repo> <bindingId> --reason '…' --expect <digest>
601	vcv binding remove <repo> <bindingId> --expect <digest>
602	```
603	
604	`--source` is required: every claim says whether an agent, a person or a tool made it.
605	`--allow-unchecked` stores a claim whose selector cannot be checked; it then verifies as
606	`unchecked`, never as `resolved`.
607	
608	A scripted run on Course Desk with the M2.3 agent draft:
609	[examples/reference-app/bindings/demo.sh](../examples/reference-app/bindings/demo.sh), recorded
610	output in [samples/m2.4-bindings/demo.txt](samples/m2.4-bindings/demo.txt).
611	
612	## What works today, and what stays unchecked
613	
614	Checked deterministically:
615	- the file exists inside the checkout, with exact case and without symlink escapes;
616	- the selector kinds and constructs in the table above resolve to exactly one artifact;
617	- the selected code changed or not (token fingerprint), including uncommitted edits;
618	- the bound model object changed or not between revisions in the checkout's history;
619	- the claim on disk is the one the writer read.
620	
621	Reported as `unchecked` (never guessed):
622	- selectors in other languages and file types (only `file` works there);
623	- files over 1 MB;
624	- non-literal paths in Nest decorators, aliased or namespace imports of `@nestjs/common`,
625	  `@Controller` with `host` or `version`, and computed member names;
626	- `describe.each` / `it.each` and non-literal test titles;
627	- namespaces and destructuring declarations, where they could hide the named symbol.
628	
629	Read-only evidence queries over these claims (by object, by claim, an overview and an explicit
630	refresh), through the CLI and MCP with one schema, are M2.5: [evidence.md](evidence.md).
631	
632	Not done by design:
633	- **Route paths are controller-relative.** A global prefix (`app.setGlobalPrefix("api")`),
634	  versioning or `RouterModule` is not applied, so `GET /courses` is the locator for a route
635	  served at `/api/courses`.
636	- **Test titles are matched syntactically.** `describe`/`it`/`test` calls are recognized by
637	  name, without checking where they are imported from.
638	- **No rename following.** VCV reports `missing` and leaves the claim alone; an agent or a
639	  person finds the new location and reasserts it. (M2.5 added read-only evidence queries, not
640	  rename hints.)
641	- **No resolver cache.** Everything is recomputed on each call. A cache, if added, goes under the
642	  git-ignored `.vcv/cache/`.
643	- **No audit entries for binding writes.** Git history is the record of who changed a claim.
644	- **Claims are not part of project status.** A conflicted claim file shows up as `invalid` in
645	  `binding list`/`verify`; the model is still served.
646
