# Model proposals and the pre-approval review (M3.1)

How a coding agent hands VCV a typed model change, and how a reviewer sees exactly what it
would change before deciding. This is the first step of the model-first path in
[Issue #17](https://github.com/TheBluemist1404/vibe-code-visualiser/issues/17):

1. the agent reads the model and the source evidence and **authors a typed proposal** (a YAML or
   JSON file of its own, outside `.vcv/`);
2. **VCV validates** it and records it as pending: `vcv proposal submit`;
3. **a separate reviewer** previews it (`vcv proposal preview`) and approves the exact digest
   with a trusted key (`vcv review approve`, see [approvals.md](approvals.md));
4. only an approved change becomes the next canonical `.vcv/` revision; implementation comes
   after that (M3.3).

Design notes: [ADR 0008](adr/0008-model-first-changes.md).

## Submitting: proposal-only

```sh
vcv proposal submit <checkout> <change.yaml> [--json]
```

The change file is the existing typed change shape (`ModelEngine.propose`, see
[ir-v0.2-conformance.md](ir-v0.2-conformance.md)):

```yaml
changeId: chg-cancel-enrollment      # yours to choose; used once, never reused
projectId: prj-course-desk
expectedRevision: rev-1              # the revision you read; stale proposals are refused
rationale: A student can cancel a confirmed enrollment and is notified.
operations:
  - type: createCapability
    capability: { id: cap-cancel-enrollment, kind: capability, owner: mod-enrollment, name: Cancel an enrollment, initiatorActorId: act-student }
  - type: setRuleStatement
    ruleId: rul-announce-every-decision
    statement: Each enrollment decision or cancellation results in exactly one notification to the student.
```

Operations: `createModule`, `createEvent`, `createCapability` (new in M3.1), `createRule`,
`addDataAttribute`, `addState`, `addTransition`, `renameObject`, `renameState`, `linkContract`,
`setModuleDependencies`, `removeObject`, `setRuleStatement`, `setDescription`, `approveDraft`.
There is no generic patch. The payload cannot name a proposer, approver or status.

A proposal may also carry an `implementation` request: `behavior`, `acceptanceCriteria`, optional
`suggestedTests` and `scope` (repository-relative paths or globs). It is shown in the preview and
covered by the proposal digest, so the reviewer approves it together with the operations; the
engine never reads it. After approval it becomes the implementation handoff
([implementation.md](implementation.md)).

`submit` is **proposal-only**. It narrows whatever permissions the host holds to
`model:propose` before calling the engine, so the result is always one of

| Status | Recorded? | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `pending` | yes | Validated against the current revision; waiting for a separate reviewer. `.vcv/HEAD` did not move. |
| `rejected` | yes, for a well-formed proposal that fails validation (the record keeps the diagnostics); no, for a schema error, a replayed change ID or an oversized proposal | Fix it and submit under a **new** change ID. |
| `denied` | no | The host may not propose. |

It never applies or approves, even for a host holding `model:apply` and `model:approve`, and the
result reports `.vcv/HEAD` before and after the call (always equal). `vcv propose <store>` keeps
its old behavior for hosts that apply directly; give agents `vcv proposal submit`.

Limits on this surface: at most 100 operations and 256 KB (canonical JSON) per proposal.

Each diagnostic has `code`, `severity`, `path`, `message` and, for the common codes, a `hint`
saying what to do (`STALE_REVISION`: re-read and resubmit against the current revision;
`DUPLICATE_CHANGE`: change IDs are immutable, pick a new one; `TARGET_MISSING`, `UNKNOWN_REF`,
`ID_IN_USE`, `REFERENCED`, `DEPENDENCY_CYCLE`, `SCHEMA`, `TOO_LARGE`, ...).

### Proposal identity

A proposal is identified by its change ID (used once; a replay never overwrites the original
record) and by its **proposal digest**: sha256 over the canonical JSON of the change exactly as
submitted. The digest is derived, never stored, and the same for a dry run and for the recorded
proposal, so a reviewer can bind a decision to the content they saw (`vcv review approve --digest`, see [approvals.md](approvals.md)).

## Reviewing: preview

```sh
vcv proposal preview <checkout> <changeId> [--json] [--limit n]
vcv proposal preview <checkout> --file <change.yaml> [--json]      # dry run, nothing recorded
```

MCP (`vcv-mcp --repo <checkout>`): `vcv_preview_proposal` with `{ changeId }` or `{ change }`.

Read-only: nothing is written, not even store recovery. The result has

| Section | Content |
|---|---|
| `proposal` | change ID, digest, origin (`record` or `unsubmitted`), lifecycle, proposer, base revision, rationale, one line per operation |
| `validation` | the engine's own `checkChange` against this checkout's revision **now** (`appliesToCurrent`, errors and warnings with hints), and the diagnostics stored at submission |
| `delta` | the object-level before/after change: added, removed and modified objects with the changed fields (values capped at 300 characters). Against the current revision when the change applies; against its base revision when it is stale; `null` when it applies to neither |
| `impact` | modules owning a changed object (`changed`) or a structural impact candidate (`impacted`), `crossModule` (`yes`, `no`, or `not-determined` when only one module was seen but the candidate list was cut), contracts, and `@vcv/query` impact candidates with one dependency path each |
| `bindings` | binding claims on changed, removed or impacted objects: code that probably has to change too. Listed, not verified; use `vcv evidence` for their state |
| `states` | `change` (lifecycle), `approval` (`none`, `applied-by-host`, `approved-by-separate-reviewer`), `snapshotStatus` and `implementation`, kept apart |
| `assumptions` | what nobody has checked: structural impact is not semantic proof, the code was not compared, the proposer identity is a host assertion, and case-specific ones (no rationale, stale, cross-module, truncated, no claims) |

Every list is capped by `limit` (default 50, max 200) with `total` and `truncated`.

**One observation per call.** A preview (and a listing) reads the project status, the model and
its history, the change records and, for a preview, the binding claims once, and reports only
what it read then; `context` describes that same revision. Before answering it checks the store
fingerprint, the Git commit, the change records and the claim files again. If anything moved (a
`git checkout`, an edit of `.vcv/`), the call fails with `STATE_CHANGED` and nothing is mixed:
retry. There are no locks, watchers or writes.

**Untrusted files are not followed.** HEAD, revision files and change records are read only as
regular files (never through a symlink, never a FIFO or device), up to a size bound (4 MB HEAD,
8 MB revision, 1 MB change record), and `revisions/` and `changes/` must be plain directories.
An entry that breaks this, or a change record that is not valid JSON for its own ID, makes the
project `invalid` everywhere (status, CLI, MCP, the writer), naming the file: recovery relies on
reading every applied record, so it cannot be skipped. A readable record whose `change` is not a
typed change only shows as lifecycle `invalid`; the project stays usable.

## Lifecycle and the states that must not be confused

```sh
vcv proposal list <checkout> [--states pending,stale,rejected,applied,invalid] [--json]
```

MCP: `vcv_list_proposals`. The lifecycle is derived from the record and this checkout's model
every time; it is never stored:

| Lifecycle | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `pending` | validated, awaiting a separate reviewer; base revision is the current one |
| `stale` | still pending, but the checkout's model is no longer its base: `superseded` (the base is an earlier revision of this line) or `other-line` (the base is not in this checkout's history, e.g. a record from another branch). An approval would fail with `STALE_REVISION`; submit a new proposal |
| `rejected` | failed validation at submission or when an approval rechecked it |
| `applied` | committed as a model revision; `resultInThisCheckout` says whether this checkout's history contains it |
| `invalid` | the record file does not hold a typed change |

Four things are reported separately and none implies another:

- **change approval** (`approval`, `recordedApproverId`): what the change record says.
  `applied-by-host` means it was applied without a separate approver (a host with
  `model:apply`, or a self-approval the policy allowed); `approved-by-separate-reviewer` means
  the record names an approver other than the proposer. Either way a record in a Git
  repository is not proof that a particular person approved it; a signed attestation checked by
  `vcv integrity` is ([approvals.md](approvals.md)).
- **snapshot status** (`snapshotStatus`, draft or approved): the model's own `approveDraft`
  flag. Approving a change does not approve a draft snapshot, and vice versa.
- **binding resolution** (`vcv evidence`): whether a pointer into the code resolves. Not model
  approval, not correctness.
- **implementation**: always `not-recorded` here. VCV never infers that approved intent was
  implemented; the implementing agent's report is a separate claim
  ([implementation.md](implementation.md)).

## What this does not do

No MCP write tools (submission is the host's CLI), no approval here (that is
`vcv review approve`, [approvals.md](approvals.md)), no implementation handoff
(M3.3), no reconciliation of code and model (M4). VCV never writes a proposal itself: the agent
authors it, VCV validates and records it.
# Maintaining a VCV model after the code changed

This guide is for a coding agent (or a person) keeping an existing VCV model in line with a
repository whose code has changed. It is general: it says nothing about any particular
application. It assumes the repository already has a `.vcv/` project and binding claims.

**Who does what.**

| | does | does not |
|---|---|---|
| **You** | read the evidence, inspect the code, decide what the change means, and propose a typed model change | edit `.vcv/` files, approve your own change, or present a guess as a fact |
| **VCV** | reports which claims still resolve and whether their code or model object changed; validates your proposal and stores it as pending | analyse what code means, infer a model change, edit the model by itself, or watch the repository |
| **A person** | reviews and approves (or rejects) the pending proposal | |

`vcv` below is the VCV command line. In a VCV checkout it is
`npm run vcv -- <args>` (or `node --experimental-strip-types apps/cli/src/main.ts <args>`).
The same evidence is available over MCP (`vcv-mcp --repo <checkout>`, tools
`vcv_get_evidence_overview`, `vcv_get_object_evidence`, `vcv_get_binding_evidence`,
`vcv_refresh_evidence`) with identical requests and results.

## Workflow

1. **Check the project.** `vcv project status .` must report `ready`. Note the model revision
   (for example `rev-1 [draft]`) and whether the working tree is dirty.
2. **Recheck the evidence.** `vcv evidence . refresh` recomputes every claim against the working
   tree now and prints counts by state and an `observationToken`. Nothing runs in the background:
   evidence is only as new as your last call.
3. **List what needs a look.** `vcv evidence . overview --states stale,missing,ambiguous,indeterminate,invalid`.
   For each model object named there, `vcv evidence . object <id>` shows every claim about it,
   and `vcv query .vcv context <id>` shows the model's current record of it.
4. **Inspect the code yourself.** `git status`, `git diff` and `git log` show what changed; read
   the files named in the claims' locators and the tests. Evidence tells you *where* to look and
   *that* something changed, never *what it means*. A claim's `locator.detail` and
   `freshness.*.cause` say why it is in its state.
5. **Decide what is no longer true in the model.** Compare each affected object's record (its
   statement, description, attributes, states) with the code. Model what the code does now. If
   the code and its tests disagree, or you cannot tell, say so instead of choosing.
6. **Write one proposed change** to a file outside `.vcv/` (for example
   `vcv-maintenance/change.yaml`) using the operations below, with `expectedRevision` set to the
   current model revision and a `rationale` that cites the code.
7. **Submit it**: `vcv propose .vcv vcv-maintenance/change.yaml`. As an agent you can propose but
   not apply, so a valid change is stored as `pending` for a person. `rejected` comes with
   diagnostics: fix the change file and submit again under a new `changeId`. Do not try to
   approve it; an approval attempt by the proposer is denied.
8. **Check again.** `vcv evidence . refresh --since <token>` should still report the same
   claims as stale or missing: a pending proposal changes nothing, and claims are never updated
   by a model change. A person re-records or reasserts claims after reviewing the code.
9. **Write a report** next to the change (for example `vcv-maintenance/report.md`) that keeps
   four kinds of statement apart:
   - **Source observed**: what the code and its history show, with file paths;
   - **Agent inferred**: what you concluded it means for the model, and how sure you are;
   - **VCV validated**: what VCV reported (evidence states and causes, the proposal's status
     and diagnostics), quoted from its output;
   - **Needs a person**: the approval, claims to reassert or remove, and open questions.

Never create, edit or delete files inside `.vcv/` yourself, and do not change the source code
or the claims unless you were asked to.

## Evidence states

| State | Meaning | Usual next step |
|---|---|---|
| `resolved` | the pointer resolves to exactly one artifact, and neither its code nor the model object changed since the claim | nothing, but it is not proof the code is correct |
| `stale` | it resolves, but the selected code changed (`source: changed`) or the model object changed or was removed (`model: changed/removed`) | read the code; propose a model change if the model is now wrong |
| `missing` | the file or selector no longer resolves (renamed, moved, deleted) | find where it went; a person reasserts or removes the claim |
| `ambiguous` | the selector matches more than one artifact | a person makes the locator more specific |
| `unchecked` | outside the supported subset (see below); only the claim is reported | inspect by hand |
| `indeterminate` | it resolves but some evidence is unknown (for example the claim's revision is from another branch) | treat as unknown, never as a pass |
| `invalid` | the claim file itself cannot be read (conflict markers, bad JSON, unsafe entry) | a person repairs the claim file |

Every result says `meaning: "unverified"` and every claim `approval.approved: false`. The model's
own status (`context.snapshotStatus`, draft or approved) is a separate fact: a draft model with
resolved claims is still a draft, and an approved model with stale claims is still approved.

An edit elsewhere in a bound file is reported as `fileChanged: true` with the cause "not
evidence about this claim"; only a change to the selected declaration (its tokens, not comments
or formatting) makes a symbol, route or test claim stale.

## Change operations

A change file:

```yaml
changeId: ch-maint-01            # lowercase letters, digits, '.', '-', '_'; new for every submission
projectId: <the project id>      # from `vcv project status .`
expectedRevision: <current rev>  # e.g. rev-1
rationale: <why, citing the code>
operations:
  - type: setRuleStatement
    ruleId: rul-order-limit
    statement: An order of more than ten items is split into parcels of at most ten.
```

| Operation | Parameters |
|---|---|
| `setRuleStatement` | `ruleId`, `statement` |
| `setDescription` | `objectId`, `description` (any object with a description, and the project; not attributes, states or transitions) |
| `createRule` | `rule`: a full rule object (`id`, `kind: rule`, `owner`, `name?`, `ruleKind`, `statement` …) |
| `renameObject` | `objectId`, `name` |
| `addDataAttribute` | `dataId`, `attribute: { id, name, type, nullable?, refDataId? }` |
| `createEvent` | `event: { id, kind: event, owner, name, description? }` |
| `createModule` | `module`: a full module object |
| `addState` / `renameState` | `behaviorId`, `state: { id, name }` / `behaviorId`, `stateId`, `name` |
| `addTransition` | `behaviorId`, `transition` (see the bootstrap guide's model reference) |
| `linkContract` | `moduleId`, `contractId` (adds a consumed contract) |
| `setModuleDependencies` | `moduleId`, `dependsOn: [module ids]` |
| `removeObject` | `objectId` (refused while anything still references it) |

Operations apply in order, all or nothing, and the result must be a valid model. Prefer the
smallest change that makes the model true again; say in the rationale what you left unchanged
on purpose.

## What evidence can and cannot tell you

- Selectors are checked only in TypeScript (`.ts`, `.tsx`, `.mts`, `.cts`): named declarations,
  decorated HTTP handlers with literal paths, and `describe`/`it`/`test` titles. Everything else
  is `unchecked`. Only syntax is read; there is no type checking or import following.
- Routes are controller-relative: a global prefix or versioning is not applied.
- Test titles are matched by name; a renamed test is `missing`, even if it tests the same thing.
- VCV never follows a rename or a move. It reports `missing` and leaves the claim alone.
- `stale` says the code changed, not how. The diff and your reading decide what it means.
- A claim made against a model revision from another branch is `indeterminate` here.
- Evidence never contains source text or absolute paths, and reading it never writes anything.
# Implementation handoff and the implementation report (M3.3)

The third step of the model-first path in
[Issue #17](https://github.com/TheBluemist1404/vibe-code-visualiser/issues/17). Once a change is
approved ([approvals.md](approvals.md)), the person invokes their coding agent, with its normal
tools, to implement it in the feature checkout. VCV gives that agent a bounded brief, the
**handoff**. Afterwards it records the agent's account next to what VCV can observe, in the
**implementation report**. VCV never starts the agent, never runs the tests, and never turns code
into model operations.

Design notes: [ADR 0008](adr/0008-model-first-changes.md#m33-decisions).

## The implementation request, approved with the change

What should be implemented is part of the proposal, so the reviewer approves it together with the
operations and the proposal digest covers it:

```yaml
changeId: chg-capacity
projectId: prj-course-desk
expectedRevision: rev-1
rationale: students asked why they were rejected
operations:
  - { type: setRuleStatement, ruleId: rul-seat-limit, statement: "…" }
implementation:
  behavior: When a course is full, the rejection tells the student the course's capacity.
  acceptanceCriteria:
    - A COURSE_FULL rejection includes the course capacity
    - Enrolling into a course with free seats is unchanged
  suggestedTests:
    - "EnrollmentService: rejects an enrollment into a full course and reports the capacity"
  scope: ["server/src/enrollment/**"]
```

`scope` holds repository-relative paths or globs (`*`, `**`, `?`; a plain path also covers
everything below it). Absolute paths, `..` and backslashes are refused. The request is strict and
bounded: behavior up to 4000 characters, at most 30 criteria, 30 tests and 50 scope entries. The
engine never reads it. `vcv proposal preview` shows it, and warns when it is missing or declares no
scope.

## The handoff: `vcv handoff <path> <changeId>`

The handoff is printed as JSON. It is read-only and needs an **applied change with an
attestation whose signature verifies against its record**. Otherwise you get `NOT_APPLIED`,
`NOT_ATTESTED` or `NOT_IN_HISTORY` (check out the branch the change was approved on). Key trust
is not decided here; that is the host gate's job.

It contains:

| Field | What it is |
| ----- | ---------- |
| `change` | Change ID, proposal digest, base and approved revision, proposer, approver, rationale and operation summaries (display text, cut with `rationaleTruncated` / `operationsTruncated`; the proposal digest covers the full text) |
| `approval` | `valid-signature`, the key fingerprint, and `trustVerification: caller-asserted` |
| `modelNow` | The current revision; whether it is still the approved one; any later revisions (not covered) |
| `delta`, `impact` | The object-level before/after of the approved revisions, plus structural impact (modules, contracts, cross-module) |
| `request` | The approved implementation request, or null (a caveat then says there are no approved criteria) |
| `scope` | `declared` (the approved scope), and `fromBindings`: files that binding claims on changed or impacted objects point at |
| `tests` | Requested tests, plus `tests` claims on the affected objects |
| `bindings` | Each affected claim verified now (`resolved` / `stale` / `missing` …, with source and model freshness). `reassertAfterImplementing` marks claims on changed objects |
| `git` | Base commit, branch and dirty flag of the checkout the agent starts from, and `worktree`: a digest of the bytes seen (bound source files and files changed since HEAD) |
| `steps`, `caveats` | Fixed instructions and what the handoff does not establish |
| `digest` | sha256 over the canonical JSON of everything above |

Properties:

- **Deterministic.** There are no timestamps and the ordering is stable, so the same checkout
  state gives the same bytes and the same digest.
- **Bounded.** Strings and lists are capped, each cut marked. The printed handoff (2-space JSON,
  digest included) never exceeds 128 KiB: derived lists are halved until it fits, and if it still
  does not, the call fails with `HANDOFF_TOO_LARGE` instead.
- **Redacted.** Only repository-relative paths appear. The checkout's absolute path and the home
  directory are scrubbed from every string, including free text.
- **One observation.** Like every read surface, it reads the checkout once and rechecks before
  answering (`STATE_CHANGED`). The recheck covers the model store, the Git commit, the change
  records, the binding claims, the change's attestation, and the working tree: the set of changed
  files and the bytes of every changed or bound file. An edit during binding verification is
  never mixed into the result.

## Implementing (the agent's job)

The handoff's `steps` say it. The agent:

- works in this checkout and inspects the code itself;
- stays in the declared scope;
- never edits `.vcv/HEAD`, `revisions/`, `changes/` or `approvals/`;
- if the approved model turns out to be wrong, stops and starts a **new** proposal and review;
- re-inspects and **reasserts** every claim marked `reassertAfterImplementing`
  (`vcv binding reassert … --expect <digest>`, or `vcv binding add` for new code). Reassertion is
  its claim, not an approval;
- runs the tests and writes down what really happened.

## The report: `vcv implementation record <path> --report <file> [--expect <digest>]`

The agent writes a JSON file of its own:

```json
{
  "changeId": "chg-capacity",
  "baseCommit": "<git.baseCommit from the handoff>",
  "handoffDigest": "<digest from the handoff>",
  "testsRun": [{ "command": "npm test -w server", "outcome": "passed", "summary": "12 passed" }],
  "acceptance": [{ "criterion": "A COURSE_FULL rejection includes the course capacity", "status": "met", "evidence": "enrollment.service.ts" }],
  "gaps": ["the web UI does not show the capacity yet"],
  "outOfScope": [{ "path": "README.md", "reason": "documented the new message" }],
  "confidence": "medium"
}
```

VCV records `.vcv/implementations/<changeId>.json` (commit it with the code). The report keeps
four sections apart, and none implies another:

- **`approvedIntent`**: the approved request and operations, from the change record.
- **`agentClaims`**: tests, outcomes, criteria, gaps, explanations and confidence, with
  `claimedBy` (the host-asserted principal) and `verifiedByVcv: false`. VCV ran nothing and
  verified none of it.
- **`vcvObserved`**: what VCV sees:
  - source files changed since the base commit (committed, staged, unstaged and untracked);
  - those outside the approved scope;
  - `.vcv/` changes by area;
  - `worktree`: a digest of the bytes of every changed and bound file (content hashes, or size and
    mtime past the budget, then `complete: false`), so the report names one concrete dirty source
    state, not only file names. A path through a symlink is resolved like the binding verifier
    resolves it (inside the checkout only) and identified by its target's bytes, Git-ignored
    targets included;
  - each affected binding claim verified now, with `reasserted` (claimed at the approved revision
    or later).
- **`notReconciled`**: always `not-reconciled`. Whether the code implements the model is M4's
  reconciliation.

It **warns rather than passes silently**:

| Warning | When |
| ------- | ---- |
| `OUT_OF_SCOPE` | A file changed outside the approved scope; listed even when the agent explains it |
| `SCOPE_NOT_DECLARED` | The approved request declared no scope |
| `NO_IMPLEMENTATION_REQUEST` | The approved change carried no request |
| `NO_SOURCE_CHANGES` | No source file changed since the base commit |
| `BINDING_NOT_RESOLVED` | An affected claim is not `resolved` now |
| `BINDING_NOT_REASSERTED` | A claim on a changed object was last made before the approved revision |
| `NO_BINDINGS` | No claim points at the affected objects |
| `TEST_FAILED` | A reported test failed or errored |
| `NO_TESTS_RUN` | The agent reports no test run |
| `CRITERION_NOT_MET` / `CRITERION_UNKNOWN` | The agent reports a criterion as not met or unknown |
| `CRITERION_UNADDRESSED` | An approved criterion is not addressed in the report |
| `GAP` | The agent's own gaps |
| `MODEL_MOVED` | The model is past the approved revision |
| `STORE_FILES_CHANGED` | Unexpected `.vcv/` files changed |
| `CLAIMS_UNVERIFIED` | Always present |

Recording changes no model state. The base commit must be in the repository and an ancestor of
HEAD (`UNKNOWN_COMMIT`). A second report is refused (`REPORT_EXISTS`). To replace a report, pass
the current file's digest with `--expect` (`REPORT_CHANGED` if it moved, including when another
report is written while the replacement is prepared: the file is re-read right before the
rename). A symlinked or non-directory `.vcv/implementations/` is refused (`UNSAFE_PATH`). Reports
are bounded to 256 KB and redacted like the handoff. Recording rechecks the same state as the
handoff (store, commit, records, claims, attestation, changed files and their bytes) before it
writes (`STATE_CHANGED`).

`vcv implementation show <path> <changeId>` reads a report and recomputes VCV's observations now.
The stored report is validated against the full report schema first; a malformed or foreign file
is `INVALID_RECORD`, with the failing fields. `changedSinceReport` says whether the files, their
bytes, the scope or the binding states moved on since the report was recorded (an edit of an
already-dirty file counts), and `warningsNow` lists the warnings as they stand now.

## What this does not do

- No universal implementation verifier.
- No agent orchestration or hidden trigger of code generation.
- No test execution by VCV.
- No automatic model operations from code.
- No MCP tools for these (the agent uses the CLI it already has).
- No reconciliation (M4).

The report is evidence for a human reviewer of the PR, not a gate.
# Source bindings (M2.4)

A **binding claim** says that a piece of source code implements, exposes, persists or tests an
object in the model. An agent or a person makes the claim. VCV stores it, checks it and shows it.
VCV does **not** decide whether the code does what the claim says.

Design contract: [ADR 0007 §§4–6](adr/0007-repository-projects.md). Tracking issue:
[#13](https://github.com/TheBluemist1404/vibe-code-visualiser/issues/13).

## Three different things

| | Who supplies it | What it means | What it does not mean |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Claim** | an agent or a person, through `vcv binding add` / `reassert` | "this code is that model object", plus who said so, when (model revision, Git commit) and why | that VCV checked the meaning, or that the code is correct |
| **Verification** | VCV, recomputed on every `vcv binding verify` | the pointer resolves to exactly one artifact, and whether that artifact or the model object changed since the claim | anything about behaviour. Every result carries `meaning: "unverified"` and `approved: false` |
| **Approval** | a person, through the model engine | a consequential model decision was accepted | binding claims are never approved by verification, and recording a claim never changes the model |

Recording a claim does not make a draft model approved, and does not set the query API's
`implementationChecked` (it stays `false`).

## Where claims live

One file per claim: `.vcv/bindings/<bindingId>.json`, tracked by Git like the code. Git is the
only history: there is no binding revision counter, and no binding operation touches
`.vcv/HEAD`, the model revisions or the change records. A source edit and the matching claim
update can go into one commit.

```json
{
  "format": 1,
  "bindingId": "impl.cap-enroll",
  "modelObjectId": "cap-enroll",
  "relation": "implements",
  "locator": { "path": "server/src/enrollment/enrollment.service.ts", "selector": { "kind": "symbol", "name": "EnrollmentService.enrollStudent" } },
  "provenance": { "source": "human", "principalId": "user:reviewer" },
  "modelRevision": "rev-1",
  "observed": {
    "commit": "917dffb9a9d4…",
    "workingTree": "modified",
    "fingerprint": { "algorithm": "vcv-fp-1", "file": "ceb0308c…", "selector": "418a1198…" }
  }
}
```

(full file: [samples/m2.4-bindings/impl.cap-enroll.json](samples/m2.4-bindings/impl.cap-enroll.json))

- `bindingId` uses the persisted-ID grammar. If you leave it out, it is derived from the relation,
  the object ID and a hash of the locator, so the same claim made on two branches has the same ID
  and the same bytes. It is kept when the claim is reasserted.
- `provenance.source` and `principalId` come from the host (the CLI's `--source` and `--as`),
  never from the claim payload. `confidence` is the claimant's own estimate; VCV never computes it.
- `observed` records what was inspected: the Git commit, whether the file differed from it, and
  fingerprints. There are no absolute paths and no timestamps; files are byte-for-byte
  deterministic (fixed key order).
- `disputed` is only set by `vcv binding dispute`; verification never sets it.

## Locators

A locator is a repository-relative POSIX path plus a selector:

| Form | Selector | Checked in |
|---|---|---|
| `path` | whole file | any regular file |
| `path#symbol:Class.member` | named declaration: top-level `class`, `function`, `interface`, `type`, `enum`, variable; class methods, properties, accessors and `constructor`; interface members | `.ts` `.tsx` `.mts` `.cts` |
| `path#route:POST /orders/:id` | NestJS handler: `@Controller(path)` + `@Get/@Post/@Put/@Patch/@Delete/@Head/@Options/@All(path)` with literal paths | `.ts` `.tsx` `.mts` `.cts` |
| `path#test:Suite > case` | `describe`/`suite` and `it`/`test` titles with literal strings, outermost first (`.only`, `.skip`, `.todo`, `.concurrent` are fine) | `*.test.*` and `*.spec.*` |

In JSON, a symbol selector can name its declaration kind (`"declaration": "class"`) and a route
selector its handler (`"handler": "OrdersController.place"`), to tell same-named artifacts apart.

**Paths.** A path must already be normalized. These are refused with `UNSAFE_PATH`: an absolute
path, `..`, `.`, `//`, a backslash, anything under `.git/`, `.vcv/` or `node_modules/`, and a
symlink that leads out of the checkout. A path that differs from a file only by letter case is
reported, not matched, so case-insensitive filesystems behave like Linux.

**Parser.** Only syntax is read, with the TypeScript 6 compiler API (`createSourceFile`), pinned
in `@vcv/repo`. There is no type checking, import following or project configuration. The
repository's own type checker is TypeScript 7, whose JS API is unstable and runs a native binary
over IPC, so it is not used here.

## Verification states

| State | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `resolved` | the selector matches exactly one artifact, its code is known to match the recorded fingerprint, and the bound model object is known not to have changed since the claim's revision. All evidence must be known; this is the only state `vcv binding verify` exits 0 for |
| `stale` | it still resolves, but the selected code changed (`source: changed`), or the model object changed or was removed (`model: changed`/`removed`). Someone should look again; it is not a contradiction |
| `missing` | the path or selector does not resolve (renamed, moved, deleted), or the path is no longer safe |
| `ambiguous` | the selector matches more than one artifact; none is picked |
| `indeterminate` | the selector resolves, nothing is known to have changed, but some evidence is unknown: the project is not `ready`, the claim's revision is not in this checkout's history, or the claim's fingerprint scheme is not one this VCV knows. Not a pass |
| `unchecked` | the file type or the construct is outside the subset above, so only the claim is reported |
| `invalid` | the claim entry is not a readable claim: conflict markers, bad JSON, wrong shape, a file name that does not match its `bindingId`, or an entry that is not read at all (a symlink, directory, special file, or a file over 64 KiB) |

Each result has a separate `source` and `model` freshness, each with a cause:

- **Source** compares the selected declaration's fingerprint: the sequence of its syntax tokens,
  including decorators but not comments, JSDoc or formatting. An edit elsewhere in the same file
  is reported as `fileChanged: true` with the cause "not evidence about this claim", and the
  claim stays `resolved`. A `file` selector compares the whole file (CRLF normalized to LF).
- Uncommitted edits count: verification reads the working tree, not the commit.
- **Model** compares the bound object between the claim's revision and the current one. If the
  claim's revision is not in this checkout's history (another branch), the state is `unknown`.
- **Git** context is reported (`commitMoved`, the file's working-tree state), but a moved commit
  alone never makes a claim stale.

VCV never relocates a claim. After a rename or move, the claim reports `missing` until an agent
or a person reasserts it.

## Writes are checkout-safe

Every write names the claim it expects to find on disk: no claim for `add`, and the claim's
digest (from `vcv binding list`) for `reassert`, `remove` and `dispute`. The operation then:

1. takes one snapshot: the project must be `ready`, and the snapshot holds the model store's
   fingerprint, the Git commit and the claim file's digest;
2. refuses unless the claim on disk is the expected one (`BINDING_EXISTS` for a create,
   `BINDING_CHANGED` or `NOT_FOUND` otherwise). This is how a claim read on one branch cannot
   overwrite another branch's same-ID claim after `git checkout`;
3. validates the claim: the model object exists at the current revision and at the claim's
   revision, the revision is in HEAD's history, the path is safe, and the locator resolves to
   exactly one artifact (`LOCATOR_MISSING`, `LOCATOR_AMBIGUOUS`, `LOCATOR_UNCHECKED`);
4. immediately before writing, re-checks the store fingerprint, the Git commit, the claim file and
   the source file's bytes. If any changed, it refuses with `STATE_CHANGED` and writes nothing;
5. writes through a temporary file and rename.

**Reads stay inside the checkout too.** `.vcv/` and `.vcv/bindings/` must be plain directories:
if either is a symlink, every binding read and write refuses with `UNSAFE_PATH` before reading
anything (the model itself is still served). Each claim entry is read only if it is a regular,
non-symlink file of at most 64 KiB, opened with `O_NOFOLLOW` where the OS has it and checked
again on the open file. Anything else is listed as `invalid` with a reason and a stable
`unsafe:<kind>` digest: a symlinked entry can be removed or replaced as a link (its target is
never touched), while a directory or special file under a claim's name is left for a person.
Source files for selectors are size-checked before they are read (at most 1 MB is parsed);
whole-file fingerprints are streamed in 1 MiB chunks.

As with model commits, this is check-then-rename, not a lock: a checkout landing inside the
rename itself is not prevented.

Permissions (from the host): `binding:record` to add, reassert and remove; `binding:dispute` to
dispute. The CLI grants both by default, like the model permissions.

## CLI

```sh
vcv binding add <repo> --source agent --as agent:me --object cap-enroll --relation implements \
  --locator 'server/src/enrollment/enrollment.service.ts#symbol:EnrollmentService.enroll' \
  [--id impl.cap-enroll] [--rationale '…'] [--confidence 0.8] [--revision rev-1] [--allow-unchecked]
vcv binding list <repo> [--json]                       # IDs, digests, locators
vcv binding verify <repo> [bindingId] [--json]         # exit 0 only if every claim is resolved
vcv binding reassert <repo> <bindingId> --source human --expect <digest> --locator '<new locator>'
vcv binding dispute <repo> <bindingId> --reason '…' --expect <digest>
vcv binding remove <repo> <bindingId> --expect <digest>
```

`--source` is required: every claim says whether an agent, a person or a tool made it.
`--allow-unchecked` stores a claim whose selector cannot be checked; it then verifies as
`unchecked`, never as `resolved`.

A scripted run on Course Desk with the M2.3 agent draft:
[examples/reference-app/bindings/demo.sh](../examples/reference-app/bindings/demo.sh), recorded
output in [samples/m2.4-bindings/demo.txt](samples/m2.4-bindings/demo.txt).

## What works today, and what stays unchecked

Checked deterministically:
- the file exists inside the checkout, with exact case and without symlink escapes;
- the selector kinds and constructs in the table above resolve to exactly one artifact;
- the selected code changed or not (token fingerprint), including uncommitted edits;
- the bound model object changed or not between revisions in the checkout's history;
- the claim on disk is the one the writer read.

Reported as `unchecked` (never guessed):
- selectors in other languages and file types (only `file` works there);
- files over 1 MB;
- non-literal paths in Nest decorators, aliased or namespace imports of `@nestjs/common`,
  `@Controller` with `host` or `version`, and computed member names;
- `describe.each` / `it.each` and non-literal test titles;
- namespaces and destructuring declarations, where they could hide the named symbol.

Read-only evidence queries over these claims (by object, by claim, an overview and an explicit
refresh), through the CLI and MCP with one schema, are M2.5: [evidence.md](evidence.md).

Not done by design:
- **Route paths are controller-relative.** A global prefix (`app.setGlobalPrefix("api")`),
  versioning or `RouterModule` is not applied, so `GET /courses` is the locator for a route
  served at `/api/courses`.
- **Test titles are matched syntactically.** `describe`/`it`/`test` calls are recognized by
  name, without checking where they are imported from.
- **No rename following.** VCV reports `missing` and leaves the claim alone; an agent or a
  person finds the new location and reasserts it. (M2.5 added read-only evidence queries, not
  rename hints.)
- **No resolver cache.** Everything is recomputed on each call. A cache, if added, goes under the
  git-ignored `.vcv/cache/`.
- **No audit entries for binding writes.** Git history is the record of who changed a claim.
- **Claims are not part of project status.** A conflicted claim file shows up as `invalid` in
  `binding list`/`verify`; the model is still served.
